gen-dafont-blockletter-gf-noto-sans-goth: Noto Sans Gothic opens with big, glassy counters and round, bracket-like curves. Blockletter, up top, looks drawn by a fixed-width nib, tall in the middle, while the body stays light and open.
gen-dafont-bloody-gf-noto-sans-gujarati: Noto Sans Gujarati is a sans-serif with curved strokes that stop before turning inward. Over a full page its large open counters keep lines easy on the eye, while Bloody's big round bowls stay up in the heading.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-thai: Noto Sans Thai swells into rounded, open letters that feel friendly and unguarded. Bushcraft keeps its heading shapes closed and its spacing stretched wide, so the two sit differently on the page, one tight in form, one open.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-vithku: Expressive is the first word for Bushcraft, with its wide-spaced letters and barely-there capitals. Noto Sans Vithkuqi follows with open throats on a, c, e and s, so a long passage moves smoothly with hardly any step from capital to lowercase.
